# Ascribe Coder: Getting Started

## Study Set-up

_Notes: Studies Page (modify what you see through column header filters and Table Manager/Columns Tab)_

1. Click the ellipsis on the coder icon to access the navigation drop-down.
2. Navigate to Studies.
3. Click the “Add Study” button. <img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (183).png" alt="" data-size="line">
4. Fill in Study ID and any other relevant study components.

<figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (184).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Home Page: Navigation Icon/Supervisor/Studies</p></figcaption></figure>

<figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (185).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Studies Page: Add New Study Button</p></figcaption></figure>

<figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (186).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Studies Page: Add New Study Button</p></figcaption></figure>

<figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (187).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Study Edit Dialog</p></figcaption></figure>

Data Loading/Input:


_Notes: Studies page and Ascribe Loader_

1. Format data file for loading
2. Navigate to Supervisor/Studies
3. Right click the study then choose “Load responses/ Process file” OR Click “Load Responses” action button <img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="" data-size="line">
4. Ascribe Loader Dialog:
   1. Browse to your file
   2. Choose the load option
   3. Choose auto-code options

<figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (188).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Example Data File</p></figcaption></figure>

Question Editing:


_Notes: Questions page (modify what you see through column header filters and Table Manager/Columns Tab)_

1. Navigate to Supervisor/Studies/Right click the study/Choose “Questions” OR Click “Questions” action button <img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (192).png" alt="" data-size="line">
2. Right click the question you would like to edit/Choose “Show Details” OR Click “Show Details” action button <img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (193).png" alt="" data-size="line">
3. Update relevant fields (Question text, Question label)

Codebook Sharing:


_Notes: Questions page using “Copy/Share codebook to”_

1. Navigate to Supervisor/Studies/Right click the study/Choose “Questions”
2. Right click the question you would like to share/Choose “Show Details” OR Click “Show Details” action button <img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="" data-size="line">
3. Click “Codebook” tab then click “Share To” tab
4. Select the questions to be shared
5. Click “SHARE codebook with selected questions” button

<figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (199).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Copy/Share Codebook To</p></figcaption></figure>

## Copy/Paste a Codebook from Word or Excel

1.  Format your codebook indenting for each level<br>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (200).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Excel Codebook</p></figcaption></figure>
2. Navigate to Ascribe Coder
   1. Click the Ascribe Coder Icon and access your question
   2.  Navigate to Studies/Right click the study/Choose Questions/Right click the question/Choose “Ascribe Coder” or navigate using the Ascribe Coder icon.

       <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (201).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Ascribe Coder Icon</p></figcaption></figure>

       <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (202).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Direct Navigation/Sources Dialog</p></figcaption></figure>

       <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (203).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Questions Page/Right-click Question/Ascribe Coder</p></figcaption></figure>

       <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (204).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Questions Page: Ascribe Coder Action Button</p></figcaption></figure>
3.  Unlock the codebook

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (205).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Codebook Toolbar/Locked Codebook</p></figcaption></figure>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (206).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Codebook Toolbar Unlocked Codebook</p></figcaption></figure>
4. Highlight and copy the codes from your source (word or excel)
5. Right click the (Codebook) node at the top of the right pane under the toolbar
6.  Choose “Paste”<br>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (207).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Right-click Codebook Node/Choose Paste</p></figcaption></figure>
7. “Paste text” dialog.
   1. Right click in the left pane of the “Paste text” dialog box
   2. Select “Paste”
   3. Click the “Show” button
   4. Check the display of the codes that will be inserted.
   5.  Click the “Paste into” button

       <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (208).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Paste Text Dialog: Right-click Left Pane/Select Paste</p></figcaption></figure>

       <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (209).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Paste Text Dialog: Click Show Button</p></figcaption></figure>

       <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (210).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Paste Text Dialog: Click Paste Into Button</p></figcaption></figure>

       <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (211).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Ascribe Coder/Pasted Codebook</p></figcaption></figure>

## Coding

### Search for Responses:

1. Access the Search Responses dialog box by clicking the Search Responses Icon <img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (212).png" alt="" data-size="line">. Typically, we are searching for “Uncoded Responses”.
2. Type a word in the text field to return responses that contain that word.
   1. Alternatively, leave the field blank to return all uncoded responses.
3.  Access the Word List <img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (213).png" alt="" data-size="line">. Click on a word to conduct a search for responses that contain that word.

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (214).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Search Icon/Search Responses Dialog</p></figcaption></figure>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (215).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Word List Icon/Word List Dialog</p></figcaption></figure>

### Apply Codes – Multiple methods for applying codes:

1.  Select any number of responses and click on a code in the codebook (or multiple codes).<br>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (216).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Apply Code: Selected Responses/Click Code Description</p></figcaption></figure>
2.  Drag a code to a response. Use this mode when you do not want to select responses. It works to code one responses at a time. Drag and drop does not respect highlighted responses. It’s a convenient way to apply a single code to a single response. This method comes in handy when you have selected multiple responses but need to apply a single code to a couple of those responses without it applying to all. It’s a “clean-up” tool when mass coding.<br>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (217).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Apply Code: Drag &#x26; Drop a Code to a Response</p></figcaption></figure>
3.  Select any number of codes and hit the Apply Code target <img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="" data-size="line"> for individual responses. This method requires a Responses Settings <img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="" data-size="line"> configuration. The option to display the “Apply Selected Codes Button” must be toggled-on for this method to work.

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (218).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Settings Icon/Response Settings Dialog/Responses Tab/Select Apply Selected Codes Button</p></figcaption></figure>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (219).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Apply Code: Select Code/Click Apply Selected Codes Button</p></figcaption></figure>
4.  Click the regular expression hyperlink.<br>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (220).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Apply Code: Click Regular Expression Hyperlink</p></figcaption></figure>
5.  Drag an applied code from one response to another.<br>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (221).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Settings Icon/Response Settings Dialog/Responses Tab/Select Drag Response to Copy Coding</p></figcaption></figure>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (222).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Apply Code: Drag Response to Copy Coding</p></figcaption></figure>
6.  Drag Selected Responses to Codebook - Drag selected responses to the codebook node or a net to add a code based on the responses.

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (224).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Settings Icon/Response Settings Dialog/Responses Tab/Select Drag Selected Responses to Codebook</p></figcaption></figure>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (225).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Apply Code: Drag Selected Responses to Codebook</p></figcaption></figure>

### Remove an Applied Code – Multiple methods for removing applied codes:

1.  Right click on the code and choose “Remove - This code”<br>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (226).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Remove Applied Code: Right-click Applied Code and Choose Remove This Code</p></figcaption></figure>
2.  Hit the trashcan (remove code button) ![](data:image/png;base64,) beside the code. To turn on the remove code button, access the Applied Codes tab in Response Settings. Toggle on “Remove Code Button”.<br>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (227).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Settings Icon/Response Settings Dialog/Applied Codes Tab/Select Remove Code Button</p></figcaption></figure>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (228).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Remove Applied Code: Click the Applied Code Button</p></figcaption></figure>
3.  Remove more than one applied code by selecting multiple codes (clicking to highlight green) then, right click on any selected code and choose “Remove…this and all selected codes”.<br>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (229).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Remove Applied Code: Right-click Applied Code and Choose Remove This and All Selected Codes</p></figcaption></figure>

### Swap Applied Codes:

1.  Select the codes you would like to replace. Drag a code from the codebook and drop it on any selected code. All selected codes will be replaced with the new code you dragged and dropped (unless the code you dragged and dropped was already applied to a response).

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (230).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Swap Applied Code: Drag Code to Right-click Applied Code and Choose Remove This Code</p></figcaption></figure>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (231).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Swap Codes Dialog/Click Swap Codes Button</p></figcaption></figure>
2.  Select the codes you would like to replace. Select a code in the codebook. Right click on any selected code and choose “Swap…this code and all selected codes”.<br>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (232).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Swap Applied Code: Select Code/Right-click Applied Code and Choose Swap This Code and All Selected Codes</p></figcaption></figure>

### Add a Code to the Codebook:

1. The Code Properties dialog opens from the right-click menu item Insert Code. This option is available when the codebook is locked or unlocked.
2.  Inserting a code from the Codebook Node will add the code at the top of your codebook.<br>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (233).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Adding Codes: Right-click Codebook Node then Choose Insert Code/Into</p></figcaption></figure>
3. Inserting a code from the Net has these options:
   1. Below – Inserts code below the last code of the net; the newly added code is not part of the net.
   2.  Into – Inserts code into the net, at the top of the net; the newly added code is part of the net.<br>

       <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (234).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Adding Codes: Right-click Net then Choose Insert Code/Below or Into</p></figcaption></figure>
4.  Inserting a code from the code level, adds a new code below the current.<br>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (235).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Adding Codes: Right-click Code then Choose Insert Code</p></figcaption></figure>
5.  After you have edited the properties, click **OK** <br>

    <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (236).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Adding Codes: Code Properties Dialog</p></figcaption></figure>

### Add an expression to the Codebook:

Regular expressions can be added to a codebook in two ways:

1. Edit the Regular Expression field in the Code Properties
2. Dragging a response to the codebook to create a code or edit the regular expression. Note: The regular expression field is populated with the selected response or responses if:
   1. The responses are 50 characters or less.
   2. The responses do not contain regular expression operators.
   3.  The responses do not contain multiple sentences separated by punctuation marks.<br>

       <figure><img src="../.gitbook/assets/image (237).png" alt=""><figcaption><p>Code Properties Dialog: Regular Expression Field</p></figcaption></figure>
